{{< var mission >}}

Teen Service Project (TSP) brings together community programming, applied research, and public policy advocacy around a shared concern: equitable access to meaningful service opportunities for young people.

## Why this work

Service can be a way to practice civic participation, build relationships, and contribute to a place that matters. But participation takes time, resources, transportation, and support. A meaningful opportunity should not be available only to young people who can afford to take it.

TSP develops a community-led approach to teenage service while investigating how public policy can make more substantial, voluntary, paid service opportunities accessible. Local practice can help identify questions for research; evidence can inform program decisions and advocacy.

## What guides us

**Youth leadership.** Teenagers should have a meaningful role in identifying priorities, shaping projects, and deciding how their experiences are represented.

**Community strengths.** Start with the skills, relationships, places, and knowledge already present. Young people are contributors to their communities, not problems to be solved.

**Equitable access.** Consider costs, compensation, disability access, transportation, time, language, and the responsibilities that participants carry outside a program.

**Evidence-informed practice.** Make methods visible, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and revise conclusions when better information becomes available.

**Shared learning.** Treat community adaptations and criticism as inputs to the next version of the work. Avoid treating one local format as universally appropriate.

## An existing initiative, a new foundation

TSP is being redeveloped using previously created programming concepts and materials. This alpha establishes a public home, a research workspace, and a structure for organizing those resources.

## What is being developed

- An adaptable gathering model that helps teenagers develop and carry out local service ideas.
- Resources for teens, adult facilitators, and host communities, informed by original TSP materials when available.
- A reproducible research agenda focused first on voluntary, paid national service in the United States.
- An approach to advocacy grounded in verified evidence and community experience.
